items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: And Peanuts went to Pittsburgh and came back the next day and he stayed overnight with me and my wife.

ctx.x: Wow. You get around the circuit of the jazz parties?

Yes, I did. The first one was at the Gibson one, which started — I never heard of these things but I read about them in the jazz magazines. One time at Eddie Condon’s place, Cliff Lehman, who was a drummer in those days with the bunch around Condon’s, and he said “you like music so much, there’s a jazz party in Colorado that you’d certainly like to go.” And I said “yeah I’ve heard of it.” He said “well maybe you could get to go if you write to them and ask for in invitation.” But you couldn’t get one in 1968, it…

was. And we became great friends. I saw Mattie Gibson here and she was just so delighted, and made a big fuss over me. I’ve done the same thing about her because she was important to me. And she even said now this is something different but — you might want to erase it — she said “I’ll go and speak to Dick and Thomasai, he’ll be so glad because they are not on the best of terms I’m afraid. And I said “how is he?” “He’s doing pretty well” and so forth. And his son Josh is with him and so forth. But she was very…
